general.temas: Judicial and political issues recur, particularly criticism of Federal Police reports relating to Alexandre de Moraes, featured in O Globo and Gazeta do Povo. Fiscal adjustment and tax reform also appear, as does news about Petrobras. O Estado de S. Paulo stands out for covering the diplomatic crisis between Brazil and Argentina involving Javier Milei.
general.motivo_crispacion: Tensions are concentrated around criticism of the Federal Police reports and the dispute over the proceedings against Congressman Marcel van Hattem, which pits sections of the opposition against decisions by the Supreme Federal Court. Some Gazeta do Povo headlines use particularly polarizing language. The diplomatic crisis with Argentina and disagreements over fiscal adjustment also feature prominently. Sports, business and health news bring less contentious subjects to the mix.

Folha de S.Paulo.resumen:
- A lawmaker calls for the suspension of the purchase of nine armored vehicles for the São Paulo Court of Justice.
- Venezuela presents an economic plan and estimates its debt at $237.5 billion; studies propose revising the calculation of Brazil’s CBS tax.
- The United States seeks the extradition of a cartel leader detained in Mexico; Hurb’s founder is arrested in Rio.
- Riyadh’s tallest building suffers a second attack in less than a week.
- São Paulo declares the measles outbreak over; business and entertainment news also feature prominently.
Folha de S.Paulo.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly informative, although expressions such as “in crisis” and the reference to a second attack in a matter of days add a dramatic edge.
Folha de S.Paulo.sesgo: The selection prioritizes economic, judicial and security matters, alongside health and entertainment news. There is no clear partisan political slant in the wording.

O Globo.resumen:
- A city councilwoman proposes changing the rules for honors awarded by the Rio City Council following a controversy.
- The growth of e-commerce opens a debate about product returns.
- The WHO warns of a drop of more than four years in life expectancy in Cuba between 2020 and 2025.
- Two suspects are detained after a break-in at William and Kate’s country home in England.
- The front page includes business and technology matters, treatment for lipedema and criticism of Federal Police reports.
O Globo.motivo_populismo: The headlines are mostly informative; the use of “warns” adds emphasis, while the passage about the police reports uses dismissive terms such as “ridiculous” and “absurd.”
O Globo.sesgo: The selection pays considerable attention to business, technology and management, with some pieces taking a promotional tone. It also includes explicit criticism of Federal Police reports, but no unequivocal overall political slant is apparent.

O Estado de S. Paulo.resumen:
- Two reports say Lula will not invite Milei to his inauguration; another reports the end of the Brazilian ambassador’s mission in Argentina.
- Lula summons Haddad to discuss fiscal adjustment and reprimands Lindbergh.
- Vale shares fall 5.51%; the impact of oil and tax reform on revenue is also covered.
- An Italian court postpones the hearing on Carla Zambelli’s extradition until February 2027.
- Flooding in Paraná kills two people, and a falling tree at a school in São Paulo injures five. Technology and automotive news and an events promotion round out the front page.
O Estado de S. Paulo.motivo_populismo: An informative tone prevails, although expressions such as “diplomatic crisis,” “reprimands” and “keeps people up at night” add drama; there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
O Estado de S. Paulo.sesgo: The selection highlights relations between Lula and Milei, with two reports on the possibility that no invitation will be extended, and pays attention to political and economic tensions. No clear ideological slant can be discerned from these headlines alone.

Gazeta do Povo.resumen:
- Omissions in Federal Police reports about messages relating to Moraes are called into question.
- The opposition and the Senate call for Van Hattem’s parliamentary prerogatives to be defended before the Supreme Federal Court.
- Reports cover the potential effects of fiscal adjustment and changes to inheritance tax.
- Trump prepares new tariffs and a warning is issued about a Russian project for a nuclear weapon in orbit.
- Other topics include religious news and corporate customer service practices.
Gazeta do Povo.motivo_populismo: The comparison with the “dictatorial AI-5” and expressions such as “protection or omission” and “conceal messages” use confrontational and accusatory language, although other headlines are more informative.
Gazeta do Povo.sesgo: The front page highlights matters that call Moraes and Lula’s government into question, and gives space to the opposition and the defense of Van Hattem. It also includes news of religious and business interest.

CartaCapital.resumen:
- Botafogo drew with São Paulo and remains close to the relegation zone; another club confirmed its manager would stay on for 2027.
- Paulinho will miss the Libertadores final; debates about Flamengo’s age and Scarpa’s love of books also feature prominently.
- Fux voted against the destruction of Vaza Jato evidence, Moraes recused himself from an election case and Eduardo Bolsonaro appealed a conviction.
- Petrobras announced investments and dividends; the Chamber of Deputies approved an expedited vote on fiscal adjustment and Nvidia shares rose.
- Feminist organizations asked Lula to appoint a Black woman to the Supreme Federal Court and called for greater parity and racial equity.
CartaCapital.motivo_populismo: An informative tone prevails, although expressions such as “refereeing controversies” and “Nvidia surges” add drama; there is no apparent appeal to the people against the elites.
CartaCapital.sesgo: The selection devotes considerable space to soccer, alongside judicial, economic and representation issues. No defined political slant is apparent in the headlines.

opiniones.comunista:
Today I see a class struggle behind the fiscal debate. The Chamber of Deputies approved an expedited vote on the adjustment, and industry is warning about its effects on investment. But I ask: who will foot the bill, and who will decide how the resources are used? An adjustment is not neutral if it protects the profits of big capital while threatening the rights and services of the working majority.

Petrobras is announcing investments and, at the same time, extraordinary dividends for its shareholders. I believe a strategic company should serve the collective interest, not market pressure: its resources should support the energy transition and social needs, under public and worker control. The end of the measles outbreak in São Paulo is also a reminder of why we must strengthen public health care rather than treat it as a dispensable expense.
opiniones.anarquista:
The planned purchase of nine armored vehicles for the São Paulo Court of Justice, for around 5.8 million reais, reminds me how much it costs to protect those at the heights of power. A lawmaker’s request to suspend it may open a necessary discussion, but I do not trust oversight between institutions to be enough: those who pay for these expenses should be able to decide directly on them.

I am also concerned that the Chamber of Deputies approved an expedited vote on fiscal adjustment without going through the committees. A decision with collective consequences deserves more debate, not less. In the face of the concentration of power in the hands of judges, governments and parties, I stand for communities capable of deliberating, managing their resources and supporting one another. Individual freedom needs that collective strength; it does not come from delegating everything to representatives.
opiniones.liberal:
The São Paulo Court of Justice’s planned purchase of nine armored SUVs deserves rigorous scrutiny. Security may justify spending, but those who manage public money must demonstrate that it is necessary and seek proportionate alternatives. It is not the state’s money: it comes from citizens who could spend it on their own priorities.

I am also concerned that fiscal adjustment may rely on higher taxes, as industry warns. Balancing the books is essential, but doing so by increasing the burden on those who invest and work could weaken the economic activity that sustains tax revenue. I prefer a limited state that reviews its spending, maintains stable rules and leaves room for the market. Economic freedom does not eliminate personal responsibility: it requires everyone to answer for their decisions, while public authorities are accountable for theirs.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
I am outraged that the São Paulo Court of Justice intends to buy nine armored vehicles for an estimated 5.8 million reais while fiscal adjustment is being discussed. Officials’ security may be necessary, but those who manage public money must justify every expense, not treat it as a privilege of the ruling caste.

I am also concerned that industry is warning about the burden of taxes in the adjustment. A country does not strengthen its sovereignty by punishing those who produce, invest and create jobs. And families’ concerns about changes to inheritance tax deserve respect: passing on the fruits of a lifetime of work should not become a race against the taxman. I want a strong state to maintain order and defend the nation, but one that is limited when it threatens parliamentary freedom, property and the continuity of families.
opiniones.centro:
I am concerned that the expedited procedure approved for fiscal adjustment will reduce the time available for scrutiny. Brazil needs sustainable public finances, but also a transparent debate about who will bear the costs. I take seriously industry’s warning about the impact of higher taxes on investment; I also believe that any adjustment must protect essential services and those least able to bear the burden.

The discussion about the São Paulo Court of Justice’s armored vehicles points to the same requirement: public spending must be justifiable. I trust the Court of Accounts to examine the purchase independently, without prejudging whether it is necessary. For me, fiscal discipline is not just about raising more revenue or cutting spending: it requires clear priorities, effective oversight and lasting agreements.
